subject: Meteorology
title: Cumulonimbus Clouds
description: A fast breakdown of Cumulonimbus Clouds for builders.

hook.text: Cumulonimbus is the king of clouds—towering from near the surface up to 15 km or higher.

buildup.text: It starts as a cumulus cloud that keeps growing because strong instability fuels continuous updrafts.

discovery.text: When the top hits the tropopause, it spreads into a flat anvil shape—a signature of mature thunderstorms.

twist.text: Inside, updrafts can exceed 50 m/s—strong enough to suspend hailstones the size of grapefruits.

climax.text: A single cumulonimbus releases energy equivalent to multiple nuclear bombs—all from condensing water vapor.

punchline.text: One cloud, nuclear-level energy—powered by water.

quiz.question: What gives cumulonimbus its characteristic anvil shape?
options: The top spreading at the tropopause
